claims.text: High-pressure liquid Cu infiltration of a pre-sintered porous W scaffold will produce a nearly void-free W–Cu composite.
High-pressure infiltration will produce superior W–Cu interfacial bonding relative to conventional low-pressure or uncontrolled infiltration.
The proposed composite will have enhanced thermal transport relative to conventional low-pressure or uncontrolled infiltration products.
The proposed composite will have enhanced irradiation resistance while preserving mechanical durability.
Conventional infiltration, SPS, and vapor-coating methods typically produce W–Cu material with phase separation, voids, or incomplete interfacial contact.
An externally applied pressure of at least approximately 50 MPa is suitable for forcing molten Cu into a porous W scaffold.
Processing near 1100 °C will fully melt Cu while preserving the solid W framework.
High external pressure boosts capillary forces sufficiently to overcome the natural wettability limitations between molten Cu and W.
High external pressure forces complete infiltration of molten Cu into the W network.
High-pressure infiltration closes existing voids in the W–Cu structure.
High-pressure infiltration minimizes W–Cu phase separation during solidification.
High-pressure infiltration promotes strong metallurgical bonding between W and Cu.
Reduced porosity and stronger W–Cu interfacial bonding lower interfacial thermal resistance.
The resulting interfacial structure resists irradiation-induced defect formation.
Reduced interfacial thermal resistance will improve the composite's thermal conductivity.
Compared with conventional low-pressure infiltration, high-pressure infiltration will improve post-irradiation mechanical durability.
